cot.physical_observation: A ball (mass M=1.388 kg, radius r=0.101 m, I=0.618 \cdot M \cdot r^2) is placed on a horizontal conveyor belt with initial linear velocity v_ball(0)=0.000 m/s and forward (top of ball moves +x) (\omega(0)=3.875 rad/s). The belt itself starts at v_belt_0=+0.652 m/s (+x) and accelerates uniformly at a_belt=-0.064 m/s^2 so that v_belt(t) = v_belt_0 + a_belt \cdot t. Kinetic friction (\mu_k=0.048) at the contact translates and spins the ball; the system seeks pure rolling on the moving belt: v_ball - \omega r = v_belt(t).

physical_law.name: Newton-Euler equations + Coulomb friction with a time-varying surface velocity
physical_law.statement: A rigid ball on a frictional surface whose own velocity v_belt(t) may itself be a function of time obeys Newton's 2nd law for the centre of mass (M \dot{v} = \SigmaF) and Euler's equation about the CoM (I_cm \dot{\omega} = \Sigma\tau). The only horizontal force is kinetic friction at the contact, F = -\mu_k M g sgn(v_rel) with v_rel = (v - \omega r) - v_belt(t); it has a moment arm r about the CoM, coupling translation and rotation. Slip persists while v_rel \neq  0 and is driven to zero at the constant rate \mu_k g (1 + 1/I_factor); the subsequent rolling state can be maintained iff |a_belt|  \leq  \mu_k g (1 + 1/I_factor), in which case the ball CoM accelerates at a_belt  \cdot  I_factor/(1+I_factor).
physical_law.formula: v_belt(t) = v_belt_0 + a_belt t;  M \dot{v} = -mu_k M g sgn(v - omega r - v_belt(t));  I_cm \dot{omega} = -r F_x = -F_x / (I_factor M r);  rolling sustainable iff |a_belt| <= mu_k g (1 + 1/I_factor);  in that regime a_ball = a_belt I_factor / (1 + I_factor).

equations_latex: \dot{omega} = -r F_x / I_cm,  F_x = -mu_k M g \tanh(alpha (v - omega r - (v_belt_0 + a_belt t))),  I_cm = I_factor M r^2
equations_python: v_dot = -mu_k * g np.tanh (alpha (v - omega * r - (v_belt_0 + a_belt * t)))
omega_dot = -r * F_x / I_cm, F_x = -mu_k * M g * np.tanh (alpha (v - omega * r - (v_belt_0 + a_belt * t))), I_cm = I_factor * M r**2

derivation_steps: State variables (1-D translation + planar spin about the y-axis):
x(t)     --- ball-centre x position
v(t)     --- ball-centre x velocity (= \dot{x})
\theta(t)     --- orientation angle of a visual marker on the ball (CCW from +x)
\omega(t)     --- angular velocity in the FORWARD-ROLLING sign convention (\omega > 0  \Rightarrow  top of ball moves +x)
Bookkeeping for the marker: \dot{\theta} = -\omega so a forward-rolling ball (\omega > 0) shows the marker rotating clockwise to the viewer.
Belt velocity (time-varying):
v_belt(t) = v_belt_0 + a_belt  \cdot  t = +0.652 + (-0.064) \cdot t   m/s.
Contact-point lab velocity (bottom of the ball):
v_contact = v - \omega r.
Pure rolling on the (instantaneous) belt corresponds to
v - \omega r = v_belt(t).
Slip speed of the contact relative to the belt:
v_rel = v_contact - v_belt(t) = (v - \omega r) - v_belt(t).
Kinetic Coulomb friction at the contact opposes v_rel:
F_x = -\mu_k M g  \cdot  sgn(v_rel),  regularised as -\mu_k M g  \cdot  \tanh(\alpha v_rel).
Newton-Euler equations:
Translation: M \dot{v} = F_x    \Rightarrow    \dot{v} = -\mu_k g  \cdot  sgn(v_rel).
Rotation about the CoM (axis \perp  to the page):
I_cm \dot{\omega} = (r_contact  \times  F)_y = -r F_x
\Rightarrow  \dot{\omega} = -r F_x / I_cm = -F_x / (I_factor  \cdot  M  \cdot  r).
I_cm = I_factor  \cdot  M  \cdot  r^2 = 0.618 \cdot 1.388 \cdot (0.101)^2 = 0.00883 kg \cdot m^2.
Slip dynamics (combining the two):
d v_rel / dt = \dot{v} - r \dot{\omega} - a_belt = -\mu_k g(1 + 1/I_factor) sgn(v_rel) - a_belt.
Slip-decay magnitude (a_belt = 0 limit): \mu_k g (1 + 1/I_factor) = 1.227 m/s^2.
Approximate first-rolling time (small-|a_belt| limit):
t \cdot \approx  |v_rel(0)| / [\mu_k g (1 + 1/I_factor)] = 1.045/1.227 = 0.852 s.

Belt-acceleration limit for sustained rolling.  Once rolling, the rolling constraint v - \omega r = v_belt(t) must be maintained as the belt accelerates.  Differentiating and using F_x = M \dot{v} = -r^-^1 I_cm \dot{\omega} gives
a_ball - r \alpha_ball = a_belt   together with   I_cm \alpha_ball = -r F_x = -r M a_ball.
Solving: a_ball = a_belt  \cdot  I_factor / (1 + I_factor)  and
required friction force F_static = M a_ball  \Rightarrow  |a_belt|  \leq  \mu_k g (1 + 1/I_factor) = 1.227 m/s^2.
For this run |a_belt| = 0.064 m/s^2  \leq  1.227 m/s^2  \Rightarrow  sustained rolling possible.
Reference quasi-steady-state values (a_belt = 0):
v_term  \equiv  v_belt_0  \cdot  I_factor/(1+I_factor) = 0.2490 m/s
\omega_term  \equiv  -v_belt_0 / [r(1+I_factor)]      = -3.9682 rad/s
After pure rolling is reached and the belt continues to accelerate, the rolling state itself accelerates at
a_ball,roll = a_belt  \cdot  I_factor/(1+I_factor) = -0.0246 m/s^2.

numerical_method.justification: Smooth \tanh-regularised Coulomb friction keeps the right-hand side continuous; standard non-stiff RK45 with tight tolerances captures the steep slip-to-roll transition within ~1/\alpha  \approx  0.013 m/s relative-velocity window without spurious sign chatter.

code_validation.ode_source: Newton-Euler equations of a 2-D rigid ball with Coulomb friction at the contact point; v_rel-based regularisation.
code_validation.rolling_check: At t > t \cdot the residual v - \omega r - v_belt should be < 1e-3 m/s (numerical tolerance set by the \tanh regularisation).
code_validation.energy_check: Kinetic friction dissipates relative-slip energy, while the moving/accelerating belt can supply or remove mechanical energy. After rolling is reached, energy is constant only when a_belt=0; otherwise static-friction work changes the ball's energy as it tracks the belt.

expected_behavior: During slip (|v_rel| > 0) friction drives v_rel toward 0 at the constant rate \mu_k g (1+1/I_factor) = 1.227 m/s^2; the ball's linear velocity changes by  \pm \mu_k g  \cdot  \Deltat and its angular velocity by  \mp \mu_k g  \cdot  \Deltat / (I_factor r) --- the sign depends on sgn(v_rel).
Initial v_rel(0) = -1.045 m/s  \Rightarrow  friction is in the +x direction at t=0; ball translation and spin both change in the corresponding senses.
Once v_rel  \approx  0 the contact-point velocity matches the belt surface --- this is pure rolling on a moving belt: v_ball - \omega r = v_belt(t).

For |a_belt|  \leq  \mu_k g (1 + 1/I_factor)  \approx  1.227 m/s^2 the rolling state is sustainable: ball CoM accelerates at a_belt \cdot I_factor/(1+I_factor) = -0.025 m/s^2 to keep up with the belt (this run: satisfies this bound).

Camera follows the ball, so on screen the ball appears nearly stationary while the belt's tick marks drift past it --- their drift speed is v_belt(t), so any acceleration of the belt shows up as a speed-up or slow-down of the ticks.

code:
"""
Spinning Ball on a Moving Belt — auto-generated standalone simulation.

Belt:  v_belt(t) = v_belt_0 + a_belt · t.
Ball:  Newton-Euler, Coulomb friction at the contact point opposing
       v_rel = (v - omega r) - v_belt(t).
Camera-following render; no on-frame text or numerals.
"""
import math
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.animation as animation
import matplotlib.patches as patches

                                                                              
M             = 1.3875608137581241
r             = 0.10145371890474397
v_belt_0      = 0.651571570939939
a_belt        = -0.06449611178472175
mu_k          = 0.047777739801123154
I_factor      = 0.6184749333761123
g             = 9.81
alpha_tanh    = 80.0
x0            = 0.0
v0            = 0.0
theta0        = 0.0
omega0        = 3.8752766605065645
cam_window    = 4.0
belt_thick    = 0.12
duration      = 12
fps           = 30
I             = I_factor * M * r * r

def ode(t, y):
    x, v, theta, omega = y
    v_belt_t  = v_belt_0 + a_belt * t
    v_contact = v - omega * r
    v_rel     = v_contact - v_belt_t
    F_x       = -mu_k * M * g * np.tanh(alpha_tanh * v_rel)
    return [v, F_x / M, -omega, -r * F_x / I]

t_eval = np.linspace(0.0, duration, int(duration * fps) + 1)
sol = solve_ivp(ode, (0.0, duration), [x0, v0, theta0, omega0],
                t_eval=t_eval, method="RK45", rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-11)
t = sol.t; x_arr, v_arr, theta_arr, omega_arr = sol.y[0], sol.y[1], sol.y[2], sol.y[3]

                                                                             
HW = cam_window / 2.0
y_min = -belt_thick - 0.18
y_max = 2.0 * r + 0.30

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.4), facecolor="#1a1a2e")
ax.set_facecolor("#16213e")
ax.set_xlim(-HW, HW); ax.set_ylim(y_min, y_max)
ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.axis("off")

belt_rect = patches.Rectangle((-200.0, -belt_thick), 400.0, belt_thick,
    facecolor="#3a3a4f", edgecolor="white", lw=1.2, zorder=1)
ax.add_patch(belt_rect)

N_ticks      = 24
tick_spacing = cam_window / N_ticks
tick_y0      = -belt_thick * 0.85
tick_y1      = -belt_thick * 0.15
tick_lines   = [ax.plot([], [], "-", color="#a8dadc", lw=1.5,
                        zorder=3)[0] for _ in range(N_ticks)]

ball_circle = patches.Circle((x0, r), r, facecolor="#457b9d", edgecolor="white",
                              lw=1.6, zorder=4)
ax.add_patch(ball_circle)
spoke_h, = ax.plot([], [], "-", color="#e63946", lw=2.6, zorder=5)
spoke_v, = ax.plot([], [], "-", color="#ffd166", lw=2.6, zorder=5)


def update(frame):
    cx = float(x_arr[frame]); th = float(theta_arr[frame])
    t_now = float(t[frame])
    belt_disp = v_belt_0 * t_now + 0.5 * a_belt * t_now * t_now

    ax.set_xlim(cx - HW, cx + HW)
    ball_circle.center = (cx, r)
    spoke_h.set_data([cx, cx + r * math.cos(th)],
                     [r,  r  + r * math.sin(th)])
    spoke_v.set_data([cx, cx + r * math.cos(th + math.pi / 2.0)],
                     [r,  r  + r * math.sin(th + math.pi / 2.0)])
    for i, line in enumerate(tick_lines):
        x_orig_rel = (i + 0.5) * tick_spacing - HW
        x_drifted  = x_orig_rel + belt_disp
        x_wrapped  = ((x_drifted + HW) % cam_window) - HW
        x_lab      = cx + x_wrapped
        line.set_data([x_lab, x_lab], [tick_y0, tick_y1])
    return [ball_circle, spoke_h, spoke_v] + tick_lines

ani = animation.FuncAnimation(fig, update, frames=len(t),
                              interval=1000 / fps, blit=False)
ani.save("video.mp4", writer=animation.FFMpegWriter(fps=fps, bitrate=1800), dpi=120)
plt.close(); print("Saved video.mp4")
